title: UFO whistleblowers beg Trump for immunity so they can reveal 'alien secrets'
excerpt: Three high-profile UFO disclosure figures — David Grusch, Dylan Borland and Matthew Brown — have formed an unprecedented coalition urging Trump to waive their NDAs so they can reveal what they claim is classified UAP information
content:
Three high-profile UFO disclosure figures — David Grusch, Dylan Borland and Matthew Brown — have formed an unprecedented coalition urging Trump to waive their NDAs so they can reveal what they claim is classified UAP information

06:00 ET, 03 Oct 2026

UFO whistleblowers are imploring President Donald Trump to grant them immunity so they can expose what they allege are "alien secrets" hidden behind lifelong government gag orders.

‌

Three of the most prominent figures in the so-called disclosure movement — David Grusch, Dylan Borland, and Matthew Brown — have united in an unprecedented coalition, urging Trump to waive their non-disclosure agreements (NDAs). The trio claim they gathered intelligence while operating within highly classified programs, but are legally prohibited from speaking out publicly without direct intervention from the White House.

Filmmaker and disclosure advocate James Fox spoke to the New York Post about the request, reports Daily Star.

‌

"For the first time in history you have a direct public plea, not private... to the president of the United States, to have their NDAs waived and have them protected."

He went over intent, explaining it's so the three men can "disclose what they know to the American population, because they feel like it's that important that everyone should be entitled to know that we're not alone."

‌

"You've got some heavyweight whistleblowers willing to reveal what they know. All they need is immunity from the president. Just the stroke of a pen. He's got the authority to do it," he added.

Matthew Brown, an independent contractor for the defense industry, stepped forward on the Weaponized Podcast earlier this year with bombshell claims about a covert program he referred to as Immaculate Constellation, which he alleges is responsible for collecting UFO data across various government agencies.

"The NDAs I signed prohibit me from publicly disclosing classified information obtained through my national security work without prior written government authorization, and that obligation lasts for life," said Brown.

‌

"President Trump has the opportunity to uproot the source of deep-state corruption, reset international relations, and lead humanity into a new era of awareness and discovery by disclosing one simple fact: we are not alone," he added.

David Grusch, an Air Force officer who served as an intelligence official at both the National Geospatial Intelligence Agency and the National Reconnaissance Office, gave testimony to Congress in 2023 claiming the U.S. government has operated covert UFO crash-retrieval programs spanning decades, according to the Post.

‌

"Mr. President, give us the authorization and we're ready to go," Grusch declared in a video released by Fox. He allegedly described the evidence he has reviewed as "jaw-dropping."

"This included photographs and video of the [recovery] operations including the craft and the non-human occupants. And I've seen this evidence with my own two eyes," he explained.

"I am prepared to provide a full historical accounting to the National Security Council... and the White House chief of staff and make any supporting public statements that are authorized."

Borland, an Air Force veteran, informed Congress in 2024 that he observed a massive triangular UFO hovering and maneuvering above a NASA hangar before disappearing at high speed. Borland told the New York Post, "Disclosure has to come from [President Trump]. He needs to rip the Band-Aid off himself and needs to go out there and confirm we're not alone.

"We've recovered materials and entities — biologics."

The pressure has coincided with rapid administrative moves.

According to reports, the Pentagon issued a targeted legal waiver under direction from the Trump administration, suspending administrative and civil penalties for individuals holding classified information about Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAPs).

However, this does not give whistleblowers free rein to simply dump classified files online — submissions can only be made through official channels.

A dedicated declassification initiative known as PURSUE (Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters) has also been established, enabling whistleblowers to provide data behind closed doors to authorized representatives, who will vet and scrub it for national security concerns prior to any public release, according to the New York Post.

Despite these developments, the White House has reportedly confirmed there is currently no "presidential speech acknowledging aliens" scheduled — yet, the coalition insists that with immunity and a waiver, they can finally move what they claim is physical, non-human evidence into the official pipeline.
